rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, avoidance-driven opinion holding that USPSTF recommendations are not self-executing and must be given binding effect only through accountable Secretarial implementation/review, with an Arthrex-style prospective supervisory cure if needed. The dissent is likely to argue the statute’s text makes USPSTF ratings automatically binding and that the majority impermissibly rewrites the trigger, prompting at least one principal dissent and possible separate writings on remedy and severability.
